about: Every source of content in Daily Readings: what it is used for, how it reaches the app, its licence and how far it has been checked. Shown in Settings → About & sources.

sources.title: Orthocal — Orthodox calendar and daily readings
sources.author: Brian Glass
sources.tradition: Slavic tradition on the Julian calendar. orthocal.info says its Slavic tradition reflects the practice of the OCA and ROCOR; its own documentation says the Slavic data is compiled and checked against the OCA’s calendar (oca.org).
sources.use: Each day’s Epistle and Gospel and other readings (KJV text), commemorations, service notes and Lives of the Saints. Its fasting line is not used as the day’s rule: it is shown, labelled as the OCA’s, only where it differs from the ROCOR rule.
sources.how: Fetched for each day; the days you open or save are kept on this device
sources.licence: Free public service. Its terms for reuse have not yet been confirmed in writing.
sources.review: Ask the maintainer to confirm that a free parish app may rely on the service before any public release. ROCOR differences found so far are corrected and marked in the app and listed in the ROCOR discrepancy report; others may remain.

sources.title: The Holy Bible, King James Version (1769 text)
sources.use: English New Testament in the Scripture tab; the daily readings arrive in the same text from orthocal
sources.how: Bundled with the app (kjv/), one file per book
sources.licence: Public domain. In the United Kingdom the KJV remains under Crown letters patent (Cambridge University Press).
sources.review: Confirmed for Australia. A store release that includes the United Kingdom should note the Crown patent.

sources.title: The New Testament in the Original Greek: Byzantine Textform 2018
sources.author: Maurice A. Robinson & William G. Pierpont (editors)
sources.use: Greek New Testament (Parallel and Greek views)
sources.how: Bundled with the app (greek/), one file per chapter
sources.licence: Public domain, as released by the editors

sources.title: Η Καινή Διαθήκη — the Patriarchal Text
sources.author: Vasileios Antoniades (editor)
sources.translator: Transcribed by Maurice A. Robinson & Jussi Ala-Konni
sources.publisher: Ecumenical Patriarchate (original); transcription released by byztxt
sources.tradition: The edition authorised by the Ecumenical Patriarchate
sources.use: Greek New Testament (when the Patriarchal Text is chosen)
sources.how: Bundled with the app (greek-pt/), one file per book
sources.licence: Public domain (the 1904/1912 edition and this transcription)
sources.attribution: Patriarchal Text (Antoniades 1904/1912), transcribed by M. A. Robinson & J. Ala-Konni
sources.review: This transcription is unaccented and in lower case. A polytonic Patriarchal Text (planned for a later stage) needs a public-domain or licensed accented source.

sources.title: New King James Version
sources.use: Was offered for the daily readings in version 34
sources.how: Was fetched from bolls.life, which is not an authorised distributor
sources.licence: Copyright. Use in an app needs the publisher’s written permission.
sources.attribution: None while paused. If permission is granted, the publisher requires: “New King James Version® © 1982 Thomas Nelson. Used by permission. All rights reserved.”
sources.review: Kept switched off until HarperCollins Christian Publishing grants permission in writing. The King James Version is used instead.

sources.title: Lives of the Saints
sources.author: John Brady
sources.tradition: Follows the Greek Horologion (a saint’s date can differ from the Slavic calendar by a day or two)
sources.use: Lives of the Saints under Saints of the Day
sources.how: Delivered by orthocal.info with each day
sources.licence: Used by orthocal.info with the author’s permission
sources.attribution: Lives by John Brady (Abbamoses.com), with permission
sources.review: Confirm directly with the author before any public release.

sources.title: Sayings of the Fathers (Wisdom of the Fathers)
sources.author: Parish selection for this app
sources.tradition: Orthodox Fathers and saints; a few early Christian writers marked for review
sources.use: One saying each day on Today; saved sayings in the Prayer tab
sources.how: Bundled with the app (fathers.json), each saying with its work and status
sources.licence: Short quotations. Many English renderings come from modern translations that are still in copyright.
sources.attribution: Each saying names its saint and, where confirmed, the work and place
sources.status: In use — sourced and adapted sayings only
sources.review: Sayings whose source is not confirmed are left out unless the reader turns them on. Before public release: identify the translation behind each saying and confirm permission or replace it with a public-domain or original rendering.

sources.title: ROCOR commemorations and the parish supplement
sources.author: Prepared for Holy Dormition parish, Corrimal
sources.tradition: Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia (Old Calendar)
sources.use: Commemorations the daily data lacks, marked ✦ under Saints of the Day with their source: the Kazan Icon (22 Oct OS), the Kursk Root Icon (27 Nov OS), the Synaxis of the New Martyrs and Confessors (the Sunday closest to 25 Jan OS); and six parish-supplement entries
sources.how: Bundled with the app; skipped automatically when the daily data already has the commemoration
sources.licence: Names and dates only (facts); no text reproduced
sources.review: The ROCOR entries are confirmed by the ROCOR diocesan calendar (Australia and New Zealand) and ROCOR diocesan reports. The six parish-supplement entries are to be confirmed by Fr Dionysios.

sources.title: Worked out by the app
sources.author: Daily Readings
sources.tradition: Julian Paschalion; the fasting rule of the Typikon (chapters 32–33) as kept in ROCOR; the ROCOR Liturgical Handbook for colours
sources.use: Old Style dates, Pascha and the movable feasts, tone of the week, the season (for example “Nativity Fast — Day 12 of 40”), memorial Saturdays, the day’s fasting rule on Today and in the Calendar, liturgical colours
sources.how: Calculated on the device; checked day by day for 2026–2027 against orthocal.info (730 days) and against the ROCOR reference dates in the ROCOR discrepancy report
sources.review: Open questions for Fr Dionysios are listed in the ROCOR discrepancy report (for example the Typikon allowance for ranked saints on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday of the Apostles’ Fast).

sources.title: Literata typeface
sources.author: TypeTogether (Veronika Burian & José Scaglione)
sources.use: Scripture, prayers, hymns and sayings (Latin, Greek and polytonic Greek)
sources.how: Bundled with the app (fonts/)

sources.title: Morning and Evening Prayers; the Prologue of Ohrid
sources.author: Holy Myrrh-bearers Orthodox Church
sources.use: Morning and Evening Prayers on Today; the Prologue of Ohrid in the Prayer tab
sources.how: Link only — opens their website
sources.review: A prayer book inside the app (a later stage) needs its own public-domain or licensed source.

sources.title: Holy Trinity calendar — saints, troparia and readings of the day
sources.author: Holy Trinity Russian Orthodox Church, Baltimore, Maryland (a parish of the Moscow Patriarchate)
sources.use: Troparia & Kontakia of the Day on Today; the Holy Trinity Calendar row in the Prayer tab
sources.how: Link only — opens their calendar for the date on your phone
sources.review: Corrected in version 36: earlier versions called this “Jordanville Calendar (ROCOR)”.
sources.tradition: Russian Church, Julian calendar. This is the calendar that Holy Trinity Monastery, Jordanville (ROCOR) shows on its website (jordanville.org → Daily Orthodox Calendar); it is not published by the monastery.

sources.title: OrthoChristian.com — calendar and St Theophan’s thoughts for each day
sources.author: Pravoslavie.ru / Sretensky Monastery
sources.use: The complete list of the day’s saints; St Theophan the Recluse on the day’s Gospel
sources.how: Link only

sources.title: Azbyka.ru — full service texts for the day
sources.use: Full Service Texts in the Prayer tab
sources.how: Link only

sources.title: Parish bank details for gifts
sources.author: Holy Dormition parish, Corrimal
sources.use: Support the parish (Prayer and Settings tabs)
sources.how: Bundled with the app
sources.review: Written authorisation from the parish is needed before any public release. The app must not suggest that it is endorsed by the parish or the diocese unless that is given.

sources.title: Daily Orthodox Calendar
sources.author: Holy Trinity Monastery, Jordanville (ROCOR)
sources.tradition: ROCOR (shows the Holy Trinity calendar of Baltimore)
sources.use: Reference for checking the app (27 Nov 2026: “Fast. Food with Oil”, tone eight)
sources.how: Not linked: the page shows only the current day by the monastery’s (New York) date, so in Australia it shows the previous day until mid-afternoon
sources.review: The monastery’s printed annual calendar was not available to check; it would settle the open fasting questions.

sources.title: Diocesan calendar — ROCOR Diocese of Australia and New Zealand
sources.author: Russian Orthodox Church Outside of Russia, Diocese of Australia and New Zealand
sources.use: The Diocesan Calendar row in the Prayer tab; the readings added for the Kazan Icon and St John of Kronstadt; the tones and feasts checked for November 2026
sources.how: Link; facts checked against its calendar
sources.licence: Not reproduced in the app (Scripture references only)
sources.review: Its full calendar is published through Google Calendar, which could not be read for checking; only the days shown on the diocese’s home page were checked.

sources.title: Liturgical Handbook of the Russian Orthodox Church Abroad — vestment colours
sources.author: ROCOR Diocese of Great Britain and Western Europe
sources.use: The liturgical colour of the day
sources.how: Rules applied on the device
sources.review: The handbook notes limited variations within ROCOR. No colour guide from the Australian and New Zealand diocese was found; Fr Dionysios may wish to confirm.

sources.title: Typikon — the rules of fasting (chapters 32–33), with the Nativity Fast table
sources.author: Translated by Reader Daniel Olson
sources.publisher: St Nicholas Russian Orthodox Church, McKinney, Texas (orthodox.net)
sources.tradition: Russian Typikon as kept in ROCOR
sources.use: The fasting rule; the ranked days of the Nativity Fast; the Kursk Root Icon note
sources.how: Rules applied on the device
sources.review: The table and the text differ in two places (noted in the ROCOR report).

sources.title: Fasting table (lay practice)
sources.author: St George Russian Orthodox parish (ROCOR), Sydney
sources.tradition: ROCOR parish, Australia — a common Russian lay table
sources.use: Compared only; it is more lenient than the Typikon in the Apostles’ and Nativity Fasts (fish on Tuesdays and Thursdays)
sources.how: Not used
sources.review: Which convention the parish should follow is for Fr Dionysios to decide.

sources.title: Prayer Book (the Jordanville Prayer Book)
sources.author: Compiled by Holy Trinity Monastery
sources.use: Not used yet — the candidate source for the prayers in Phase 2
sources.licence: Copyright © Holy Trinity Monastery. Quoting more than 400 words from one work needs the publisher’s permission (web form); a royalty may be charged.
sources.review: Request written permission before any prayer text is added (Phase 2).
